speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I’m Dr. Agent. Can you describe what happens when you wake up frightened, and do you remember any specific dreams or nightmares?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you recall any specific content of the nightmares, and have you experienced any recent stressors or changes in your routine? I also need to know if you have any other symptoms like headaches, vision changes, or snoring during the night.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you snore loudly or stop breathing during your sleep, and have you noticed any daytime sleepiness or behavioral changes at school? I also need to know if you have any history of allergies or a small throat opening.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Met all developmental milestones with no significant medical history. Social history: Attends school regularly, with usual playing habits and interactions with peers. Lives with both parents.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of allergic rhinitis or adenotonsillar hypertrophy, as these can cause obstructive sleep apnea? I will also request an overnight polysomnography to evaluate for sleep-disordered breathing. REQUEST TEST: Polysomnography

speaker: Doctor
text: Since she recalls the dream content and is not confused upon waking, this points toward nightmares rather than night terrors. I need to rule out anxiety; are you currently worried about school, friends, or any events at home?

speaker: Patient
text: No significant findings in other systems. No history of trauma or significant stress identified.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the absence of stressors and the clear recall of dream content, this clinical picture is consistent with a nightmare disorder. DIAGNOSIS READY: Nightmare Disorder
